title: Highly porous carbons from hydrochar by means of a controlled physical activation process and their hydrogen storage performance
material_description: CPS-820–55 | pistachio shells directly carbonized (850 C, 1 h, N2), washed with 15% HCl, then CO2-activated at 820 C (6 h) to burn-off 55%
purification_method: 15% HCl wash for one day, hot water wash, dried 120 C 2 h
activation_method: CO2 activation, vertical tube furnace, 820 C, 6 h, burn-off 55%
source_location: Table 2 (main p.4), row CPS-820–55, 5 bar column
notes: temperature printed as -196 C (converted to 77.15 K); BET area (N2, -196 C, ASAP 2020, BETSI software) 1586 m2/g; Vp at P/P0 0.95 (N2); Vmicro from cumulative 2D-HS-NLDFT pore volume (N2); Table S2 composition C 95.57, O 3.78, H 0.46, N 0.19 wt%
extractor: dual extraction A (claude-sonnet-5-5) and B (claude-opus-5-5), reconciled by C (claude-opus-5-5)
basis_evidence: Conversion from excess to total uptake was performed using the total pore volume derived from porosimetry. All H2 isotherms and reported uptake data are in terms of the total adsorption.
free_volume_calibration: He skeletal density (Micromeritics Accupyc II, room temperature) used to convert net to excess uptake (buoyancy correction); excess converted to total with N2 total pore volume

activation_method: CO2 activation, vertical tube furnace, 855 C, 19 h, burn-off 60% (N2 heating, CO2 flow 230 mL/min)
source_location: Fig. 4a (main p.7), series CPS230-855-60, digitized marker
notes: temperature printed as -196 C (converted to 77.15 K); BET area (N2, -196 C, ASAP 2020, BETSI software) 2174 m2/g; Vp at P/P0 0.95 (N2); Vmicro from cumulative 2D-HS-NLDFT pore volume (N2); Table S2 composition C 97.36, O 2.20, H 0.31, N 0.13 wt%; archive: Fig4a_CPS230-855-60.json
extractor: dual extraction A (claude-sonnet-5-5) and B (claude-opus-5-5), reconciled by C (claude-opus-5-5)
basis_evidence: Conversion from excess to total uptake was performed using the total pore volume derived from porosimetry. All H2 isotherms and reported uptake data are in terms of the total adsorption.
free_volume_calibration: He skeletal density (Micromeritics Accupyc II, room temperature) used to convert net to excess uptake (buoyancy correction); excess converted to total with N2 total pore volume

purification_method: 15% HCl 1 day, hot distilled water, dried 120 °C 2 h (after carbonization, before activation)
activation_method: CO2 physical activation 845 °C, 28 h (CO2 230 mL/min after heating under N2 at 5 °C/min); burn-off 74%; BO/t 2.64 wt%/h
source_location: main p7, Fig. 4b, series CES250w-845-74 (marker at 10.1 bar)
notes: archive: fig4b_CES250w-845-74.json. Markers of this curve below 10 bar overlap markers of other series and could not be separated (see log.md); isotherm_point_count counts the markers at >=10 bar (incl. ones hidden under other series) and is a lower bound. T printed as -196 °C (77.15 K). Basis total, defined as excess plus gas in the N2 total pore volume. H2 degas in situ 200 °C (ramp 10 °C/min) 4 h; base vacuum <1e-6 mbar (not stated as the degas end pressure, not stored); sample dry mass >20 mg (bound, not stored); H2 grade BIP+ (Air Products), purity not stated numerically. BET by BETSI software, P/P0 range and consistency criteria not stated; Vp single point at P/P0 0.95 (N2), Vmicro from 2D-HS-NLDFT cumulative curve (N2).
extractor: dual extraction A (claude-sonnet-5-5) and B (claude-opus-5-5), reconciled by C (claude-opus-5-5)
basis_evidence: "Net uptake was converted to excess uptake using skeletal (He) densities measured on a Micromeritics Accupyc II. ... Conversion from excess to total uptake was performed using the total pore volume derived from porosimetry (see Section 2.2) [23]. ... All H2 isotherms and reported uptake data are in terms of the total adsorption." (main p3, Section 2.3)
free_volume_calibration: buoyancy correction with skeletal (He) density, Micromeritics AccuPyc II, room temperature
